dossier.public_summary: The 13-day dip is not steady: most sectors show no dip while three sectors show dips 6-10 times deeper. The folded signal is dominated by a handful of very deep outlier transits, with individual depths inconsistent with a planet. A marginal secondary dip, V-like shape and strong 4-day starspot variability point to systematics from a spotted/active star rather than a 1.6 Earth-radius planet. The best explanation is a few bad transits / blended variability, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes 698.3% between sectors, from consistent non-detections (-292 to ~60 ppm) to very deep sectors (2310, 1532, 1413 ppm). Sector_depths_by_source says changes_within_a_source (SPOC 2-min p_constant 4.5e-30), so not calibration: a real depth change.

Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent (chi2 884.85 dof 27). The 3 deepest transits at epochs -48/-47/-46 carry 0.861 of the folded signal, i.e. the dip is a few (3.16x) false events, not a steady 350 ppm transit. A planet requires p_consistent near 1.

Favoring a blended/variable correction: a marginal secondary at phase ~0.55 with depth ~0.31x dip (snr 5.24 just above brightening), V-like shape (v_sigma 2.031), and extremely deep spot modulation (4.215 d period, 22k ppm amplitudes, signal at 3.16x rotation). xgboost planet_rank 0.19 also planet-unlike. Centroid verdict inconclusive and neighbours could_cause 8 (though plausible_within_1px 0) is consistent with catalogue artifacts, not a consistent on-target planet.
